findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are hard-coded in plaintext Lambda environment variables. Anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration or read access to the state file / console can retrieve these long-lived credentials and impersonate the associated IAM principal.

findings.issue_category: missing encryption of sensitive env vars
findings.description: No kms_key_arn is configured, so environment variables (which contain secrets here) are encrypted only with the default AWS-managed key and are displayed in cleartext to any principal with function read permissions. A customer-managed CMK with restricted key policy would provide a separate authorization boundary.
The function uses the nodejs12.x runtime, which has reached end of life and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving the execution environment exposed to unpatched vulnerabilities.

The function has no vpc_config, so it runs outside any customer VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security-group or NACL egress controls, which facilitates data exfiltration if the function is compromised.

The Lambda service trust policy allows sts:AssumeRole by lambda.amazonaws.com with no aws:SourceAccount or aws:SourceArn condition, providing no scoping of which account or function may assume the role.
